answer: An agent economy can blunt Sybil attacks by making trust cost something: each agent locks a bond that stays at risk while it builds reputation, and any cheating slashes it. To win influence an attacker must post a fresh bond per fake identity, so the bill rises with every clone. That hard shell, like a walnut, guards an oasis of honest trade; a lagoon of cheap fake accounts still cannot drain it, for each one must first carry its own weight in stake.
